title.value: Defining ‘actionable’ high-costhealth care use: results using the Canadian Institute for Health Information population grouping methodology
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned in the document header and abstract.
title.quote: Defining ‘actionable’ high-costhealth care use: results using the Canadian Institute for Health Information population grouping methodology

analysis.description: The study focuses on defining high-cost healthcare users in Saskatchewan, Canada using the CIHI Population Grouping methodology to segment the population into health profile groups. The research aims to identify actionable information on risk factors associated with high-cost healthcare use, particularly focusing on socio-economic status as a determinant.

type.justification: The study involves empirical analysis of health care utilization data using methodologies for population segmentation and multivariable regression models.
type.quote: The Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) Population Grouping methodology was used to define mutually exclusive and clinically relevant health profile sub-groups.

name.justification: The research involves the use of health information technologies and methodologies to address healthcare utilization and cost analysis.
name.quote: The Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) population grouping methodology enables health system planners and policy-makers to use evidence to support decision-making.

name.justification: The study focuses heavily on cost analysis of healthcare services and the economic implications of high-cost health care users.
name.quote: High-cost user studies can overlook health equity considerations, even when segmenting the population into meaningful sub-groups based on disease profiles.

name.justification: The research seeks to analyze and improve healthcare services utilization by identifying patterns in high-cost use scenarios.
name.quote: CIHI’s population grouping methodology enables health system planners and policy-makers to use evidence to support decision-making.

name.justification: The CIHI Population Grouping Methodology is used to segment the population and create health profile groups, which are central to the study's analysis.
name.quote: The Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) Population Grouping methodology was used to define mutually exclusive and clinically relevant health profile sub-groups.

is_contributed.justification: The CIHI Population Grouping Methodology is an existing methodology that is used, not developed or contributed by the authors.
is_contributed.quote: The Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI) population grouping methodology enables health system planners and policy-makers to use evidence to support decision-making.

is_executed.justification: The methodology involves computational processes, suggesting execution of algorithms to segment the population.
is_executed.quote: CIHI’s population grouping methodology uses a combination of administrative health databases and provincial health registry systems to ‘tag’ each resident with any of the 239 health conditions.

is_compared.justification: The study uses the methodology as a tool for analysis rather than comparing it to other models directly.
is_compared.quote: The method uses 24 months of data to determine health conditions.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The methodology is linked to CIHI, which is mentioned as the source.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Hatcher, J., Richards, H., Homan, C., & Zhu, V. (2017). Population Grouping Methodology | CIHI.

name.quote: Due to the availability of administrative health data through in-kind support from host institutions and data-sharing agreements, this study focuses on the provincial population of Saskatchewan, Canada.
